title: TypeScript emitter + discriminator signature helpers for structured outputs (Zod / JSON‑Schema)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: ship a set of ergonomic TypeScript compiler-time and runtime helpers that allow Structured Output contracts to be declared once and used for: 1) generated TS types for the client, 2) runtime validation in the browser/node via Zod, 3) a JSON-Schema fallback for non-Zod consumers, and 4) discriminator-aware progressive/streaming parsing.

Background: teams are currently duplicating type shapes across codegen and runtime validators. Streaming responses (partial JSON objects / union cases over a stream) make validating discriminated unions brittle. We want a single surface: a declarative 'emitter' shape + lightweight adapters that bridge to Zod and JSON-Schema, and provide hints for progressive parsing of discriminators while keeping bundle size low.

Scope/outcomes: deliver a new codegen emitter shape syntax (a small DSL in the codegen template), a runtime helper package @redwood/ts-sdk/output-helpers with: type-safe adapters -> zodFromEmitter(), jsonSchemaFromEmitter(), and streamingDiscriminatorHints(). Provide migration guide, test harness, and example repo with a streaming chat demo and reranker.

Design trade-offs considered: 1) Full Zod-first approach vs emitter-agnostic: we chose an emitter-agnostic intermediate so we can emit light-weight JSON-Schema for low-footprint consumers and keep Zod as an adapter. 2) Runtime cost vs developer ergonomics: we keep adapters lazy (only compile validator on first use) to avoid initial bundle penalty. 3) Progressive parsing complexity: we expose discriminator hints rather than forcing a streaming JSON parser — consumers can opt-in to progressive parse helpers for maximum throughput.

Success criteria:
- Generated SDK packages include emitter metadata for at least three canonical model shapes (chat message union, tool-result union, search-result polymorphic type).
- Zod adapters validate both full payloads and incremental chunks via streamingDiscriminatorHints in the example chat flow.
- JSON-Schema produced passes our existing schema linter and is emitted for the hosted API docs.
- Migration guide and examples complete; two internal teams adopt in experimental mode.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: architecture sketched with Miguel (runtime) and Sofia (codegen). Decided on emitter-first intermediate representation (IR) instead of direct Zod templates.

2026-03-05 — PoC: Jesse produced emitter -> Zod adapter that maps 'discriminator' fields to z.union + refine. PoC landed in branch feature/emitter-ir. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1428
2026-03-07 — Review: PM (Eleanor) asked for backwards compatibility with existing schema naming. We added 'name' metadata to emitter nodes to maintain stable type names across regenerations.

2026-03-09 — Trade-off discussion: we debated using AJV for JSON-Schema runtime validation to cover non-Zod consumers; decided to only emit JSON-Schema and recommend AJV where needed (keeps package size small).

2026-03-10 — Streaming ergonomics: implemented streamingDiscriminatorHints() that returns a tiny index of byte offsets and discriminator token patterns to accelerate progressive parse; initial microbenchmarks show ~20% reduced tail latency for 95th percentile in our demo harness.
2026-03-12 — Security review: no PII surfaced in emitted metadata. Storage of emitter metadata in hosted catalog will be minimized (only shape hashes) per privacy guidance.

2026-03-13 — Code review: backend infra noted that the emitter metadata should include a stable schema hash for routing fallbacks; added to spec. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1443

2026-03-14 — QA: added property-based tests for union resolution and streaming incremental parse; found an edge case where nested discriminators with identical tag names required fully-qualified discriminator paths — fixed in adapter logic.
Follow-ups: write migration guide and update console schema exporter to include emitter metadata.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Zod adapter validates full and incremental payloads in CI tests. 2) JSON-Schema produced matches schema linter rules. 3) Example app demonstrates streaming union parsing with reduced tail latency. 4) No regression in existing typegen tests. 5) Code reviewed and merged into ts-sdk/main.
implementation_notes:
- Keep runtime helpers tree-shakeable: exports split (adapters optional).
- Use stable hashing (blake3) of emitter node order + names to generate schemaHash for rollout compatibility.
- Serializer must record discriminator key(s) used by generator to avoid ambiguous unions.
- Provide small migration shim for teams using old zod templates: migrateTemplateToEmitter.js
decision_log: Emitter IR (preferred) vs Zod-first: chose IR to support multiple runtime targets
Lazy validator compilation to reduce initial bundle size
Emit JSON-Schema but do not bundle AJV by default
Expose streaming hints rather than internal progressive parser to keep API flexible
